findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 2 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Biology Board shape (4 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 14 questions numbered 1-14; by section: 2.1 4, 2.5 1, 2.6 3, 2.7 2, 2.8 1, 2.9 3.

Covers the place of bacteria in classification, cell membrane and cytoplasm, genetic material and plasmids, chemical nature of the wall with Gram staining and capsule, flagellar arrangements with pili, the bacterial groups (omnibacteria, mycoplasmas, spirochaetes, pseudomonads; cyanobacteria and actinomycetes; nitrogen fixers and chemosynthetic bacteria), bacteria as recyclers, cleaners, product makers and biopesticides, normal flora, general structure of viruses, phages in genetic engineering, and retroviruses with the history of AIDS; angles chosen to differ from the chapter exercise. Book corrections followed: mycoplasmas and spiroplasmas lack walls, lophotrichous/amphitrichous as in the text, Azotobacter fixes nitrogen into ammonia and is not nitrifying.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
